sections.heading: Error Code Unification with Simulate V1
sections.summary: New positive error code groups will apply to all methods except simulate V1, which keeps its legacy negative codes until a future V2.
sections.body:
- The proposed error code catalog uses positive values with grouping, but `eth_simulateV1` already shipped with negative error codes (−38010 to −38014) in a flat range.
  - Sims posted a comparison of the proposed catalog values vs. what simulate V1 currently uses ([issue #817](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/817)).
- The main blocker has been how to unify the two schemes; conversations across multiple PRs (from Chase and Sina) have not reached a conclusion.
  - Sims attempted to reach Felix for input but received no response.
- Agreement: lightclient confirmed that changing V1's error codes retroactively does not make sense; the practical path is a sign-based check—positive codes use the new grouped scheme, negative codes use the legacy scheme.
  - This aligns with what lightclient and Felix discussed roughly two to three months ago.
  - A simulate V2 would be the proper place to adopt the new error code scheme for that endpoint.
- lightclient noted the check is simple for library implementers: positive → new handling, negative → legacy handling.
- Sims agreed and will proceed to create a PR codifying this approach; further discussion can happen in the PR itself.

sections.heading: Meta-Tracking Release Blockers (Geth PRs)
sections.summary: Go Ethereum PRs required for the release remain unmerged despite approvals on one or two; no progress since the last call.
sections.body:
- The meta-tracking release issue has been blocked for the past two calls by pending Geth PRs and a Hive PR.
- Chase reported no change: one or two Geth PRs have approval but are not merged.
  - He raised this at ACDT as well, for the same reason.
- Boma confirmed the group is effectively stuck on everything in the release list.

sections.heading: Tracing API Specification Progress
sections.summary: Tracing spec is close but blocked on full client agreement, Geth fixture generation, and Felix's validation script PR needing minor fixes.
sections.body:
- Banteg has been driving the tracing API work; all client teams except Geth are actively merging fixes.
  - Besu currently has the most open PRs, but Chase noted that is not necessarily meaningful.
  - Banteg has a draft PR in Go Ethereum to implement tracing, but is waiting for all clients to reach 100% agreement before finalizing.
- lightclient stressed that tests must live in the execution-APIs repo, not only in Banteg's external repo, and that this was a prerequisite for merging the spec.
- Test fixture generation depends on Go Ethereum: once clients agree, Banteg will update the Geth reference to point to his fork/PR branch and generate fixtures.
- A validation script PR from Felix (one in execution-APIs, one in Hive) is 99% done.
  - Chase left feedback with a couple of small issues; once Felix addresses them, both PRs can be merged.
- No EIP is required for the tracing API; Chase confirmed many existing APIs lack EIPs and this should not be a blocker.
  - The question was raised on a recent Besu call; Chase's position is that anyone can write one if desired, but it is not necessary.
- A dedicated Telegram group exists for tracing coordination; Chase offered to add Boma.

sections.heading: Nimbus EL Coverage
sections.summary: Nimbus EL is not tracked in the tracing work and currently fails roughly 70% of RPC tests; Chase will raise this with the tracing group.
sections.body:
- Boma noted that Nimbus EL appears absent from the tracing API conversations and related PRs.
- Chase confirmed Banteg does not appear to be tracking Nimbus EL.
- Chase reported Nimbus EL currently fails approximately 70% of existing RPC tests.
- Follow-up: Chase will bring up Nimbus EL inclusion with the tracing coordination group.
